name: free_body
description: A physics free-body diagram: a body (box/ball/dot) on flat ground or an incline, with labeled force arrows radiating from its center. Choose this scene for ANY request about forces on an object, free-body diagrams, Newton's laws illustrations, inclined planes, friction/normal/gravity/tension setups, or net force. Angles are degrees with 0 = +x and counter-clockwise positive (y up), so gravity is 270. All geometry (body, ground hatching, incline wedge, angle arc, arrows) is computed for you.

incline_deg.description: If set (10–40), the body sits on an incline rising to the right; an angle arc with θ is drawn. On an incline the normal force angle is 90 + incline_deg.

id.description: Short id used in element ids, e.g. "gravity".

angle_deg.description: 0 = +x, CCW, y-up. Gravity 270, normal on flat ground 90.

magnitude.description: Relative arrow length 0–1 (default 0.7). Use consistent relative sizes — e.g. friction smaller than gravity.

color.description: Optional; default ink. Convention: gravity red, normal blue.

show_axes.description: Dashed x/y axes through the body.

net_force.description: Optional dashed accent arrow for the net force.

element_ids.ground / incline: the ground line or incline wedge
element_ids.angle_arc / label_angle: incline angle arc and θ label (incline only)
element_ids.force_<id>: one arrow per force (id from the force's id, else its index)
element_ids.net_force / label_net: the net-force arrow and label (when net_force is set)

examples.request: Draw a free-body diagram of a box on the ground being pulled to the right.
Show the forces on a block on a 30 degree incline.
